clue.text: Social survey object of hagioscope?

definitions.meaning: a study of everyday British life recorded by a large panel of ordinary volunteers, begun in 1937
a hagioscope or squint is a slit in a church wall through which the altar could be watched during the Eucharist, so what it lets you do is watch that service

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about what a sociological study and an obscure church window have in common.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is whimsical: a hagioscope exists so worshippers can see the Eucharist, so its purpose is literally the watching of that service.
explanation.definitionFit: The British research project of that name was a social survey of ordinary life, while the phrase taken literally means watching the church service.

clue.text: Something to eat — for little boy little time is more than enough

parts.note: a bun is something to eat
Dan is a short form of Daniel, a boy's name cut down
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Feeding a small boy a treat, even briefly, is said to be plenty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' does two different things: it shortens the boy's name and abbreviates time to one letter; 'for' and 'is' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abundant exists in plentiful supply, more than enough for need.

clue.text: What makes whiskies all the same?

definitions.meaning: a distillery apparatus in which spirits are distilled
an adverb meaning nevertheless or even so

explanation.definitionFit: A distilling apparatus is the device for spirits, and the adverb meaning nevertheless shares that spelling.

clue.text: Work of art grabbed by girl as one could be wounded

indicators.note: something grabbed by another is held inside it, so these letters go into the girl's name

parts.note: Molly is a girl's name

indicators.note: work is read as a verb, to knead or rework, so the letters of art are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl clutches a painting as though she had been fatally hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work of art' reads as a painting; 'Work of' instead rearranges its last word, and 'grabbed by' puts the result into the girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortal wound is a fatal one, so a person could be wounded fatally, that is, in a deadly way.

clue.text: Northerner in oriental's robe? No! No!

parts.note: E stands for eastern or oriental; with the 's it gives E'S

indicators.note: the first no says there is to be none of something, so letters are taken away

parts.note: a kimono is a Japanese robe
the second no is the letters taken away

explanation.surface: Someone from the far north wearing an eastern robe is greeted with emphatic refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'No! No!' looks like an emphatic exclamation; the first is the removal signal and the second is what is removed from the robe.
explanation.definitionFit: An Inuit or other Arctic person is a dweller of the far north, a northerner.

clue.text: Clues designed to break Labour, unfortunately

indicators.note: the scrambled letters break into the other word, splitting it open

parts.note: labour means work

indicators.note: designed means arranged anew, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Puzzle clues crafted to bring down the Labour Party, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' with its capital looks like the political party but simply means toil; 'designed' scrambles the clues and 'to break' splits the toil word open.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an interjection expressing regret, used like unfortunately or sadly.

clue.text: Record holder wanting first prize, missing first, left with silver

indicators.note: missing its first letter, so the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: gold is the first prize in a competition
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A record-setter without the top medal settles for silver instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record holder' suggests a champion; it means a convict with a criminal record. 'missing first' drops G from GOLD to leave OLD; 'wanting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An old lag is British slang for a habitual prisoner, someone with a long criminal record.

clue.text: American flier is out 0, first slip's achievement

indicators.note: the plane is what the jumbled words achieve, an outcome made from them

parts.note: taken as written
the figure zero stands for the letter O
taken as written; the 's adds no letter

explanation.surface: A cricketer out for a duck while the first slip takes the catch, as a cricket report might say.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture (out for nought, caught at first slip, a fielding position near the batsman) hides an anagram of ISOUTOFIRSTSLIP signalled by 'achievement'.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lindbergh's monoplane, the first to fly solo across the Atlantic, was an American flying machine.

clue.text: Bird heard in African lake and southern sea

indicators.note: heard means the solver listens to how the words are said rather than written

parts.note: Lake Albert lies in Africa and the Ross Sea is off Antarctica

explanation.surface: A bird is heard calling over an African lake and an Antarctic sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, Albert Ross runs together into the seabird's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The great wandering seabird of the southern oceans is a bird.

clue.text: Plant love and kiss on kisser

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
X is a kiss at the end of a letter
kisser is slang for the mouth, here the lip

explanation.surface: Romantic gestures of love and a kiss planted on someone's mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link; 'Plant' as a verb fits the kissing picture but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The primula related to cowslip and primrose is a wild plant.

clue.text: Garment of polyester not cotton?

parts.note: a sleeveless vest, read as the remark that the word polyester has one T while cotton has two

explanation.surface: A question about what fabric a piece of clothing is made from.
explanation.walkthrough: The fabric question misleads: it is about spelling. Polyester contains one T, cotton two, so a garment name split as single T fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeveless athletic vest is a garment, and split in two its letters describe one letter T.

clue.text: Half sovereign kept by retiring queen of islands

indicators.note: something kept by another is held inside it
retiring means going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a rani is an Indian queen

indicators.note: half signals that only half the ruler's title is kept, the second half going

parts.note: a sultan is a sovereign

explanation.surface: Half a gold coin is held by a queen of island realms who is stepping down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half sovereign' looks like the old ten-shilling gold coin; here it is half a ruler's title, held inside the queen turned round by 'retiring'.
explanation.definitionFit: Insular means relating to or forming an island, so it is an adjective meaning of islands.

clue.text: Comment of ass in place of vicar

definitions.meaning: the loud cry a donkey makes
the English village in the song The Vicar of ..., about a cleric who changed faith to keep his post

explanation.surface: A donkey's remark heard in the vicarage.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey's harsh cry has this name, and it is also the Berkshire parish of the turncoat vicar of song.

clue.text: Gore losing head in journey needs visual aid

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: a flight is a journey by air

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: gore is blood

explanation.surface: Al Gore, demoted mid-trip, requires help to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gore' looks like the American politician; it means blood, beheaded by 'losing head' and placed in the journey; 'needs' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A powerful lamp lighting a stadium or building helps people see, so it is a visual aid.

clue.text: Supporting dog with change of second string in a severe gale

parts.note: for means supporting, in favour of

indicators.note: the second letter, A, which names a violin string, is swapped for E, another string

parts.note: a canine is a dog

explanation.surface: A backer of a dog changes its second string during a fierce storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second string' suggests a reserve; it points to the second letter of CANINE, A, a violin string name, changed to the string E.
explanation.definitionFit: On the Beaufort scale the ninth level is a severe gale, with winds of about 41 to 47 mph.

clue.text: What's happening to the world of work among those competing?

indicators.note: one piece goes among the letters of the other

parts.note: the entry for a contest is those competing in it
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A question about what is happening in working life among competitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the world of work' reads as one phrase; the definition ends at 'world' and 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Physics says the universe tends towards growing disorder and heat death, the run-down state the world is heading for.

clue.text: Retreat with defender given card?

parts.note: a back is a defender in football
a player shown a red card is sent off

explanation.surface: A football defender withdraws after being shown a card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To back off is to withdraw or retreat from a position.

clue.text: The last knight sees insect eating bird

indicators.note: one piece eating another holds it inside

parts.note: a bee is an insect
a diver is a bird

explanation.surface: The final knight watches an insect devour a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: In Arthurian legend he was the last knight left with the dying Arthur; 'sees' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Bedivere was the last of the Round Table knights, who returned Excalibur to the lake.

clue.text: Undecided jury's comment on scout

parts.note: a jury that has not yet decided is still out
a rider is a comment added to a verdict

explanation.surface: A hung jury remarks on a scout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An outrider goes ahead of a party on horseback or motorcycle, scouting the way.

clue.text: Bigwig accepts old king's backing at the end of the French cycle

indicators.note: a word that accepts another takes it inside

parts.note: a VIP is a very important person, a bigwig

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: Old King Cole is the nursery-rhyme king

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: de is French for of

explanation.surface: An important person takes on an old king's support at the close of the French Tour.
explanation.walkthrough: Old King Cole is the nursery-rhyme monarch, turned by 'backing' and taken in by 'accepts'; 'at the' are links, with the last letter of 'the' and French 'de' ending it.
explanation.definitionFit: An early bicycle or tricycle propelled by pedals was a kind of cycle.

clue.text: Dish taking part in 1?

definitions.meaning: someone watching, an observer, in the social survey at 1

explanation.definitionFit: Slang calls a good-looking person a dish, and literally one who looks is an observer in that survey.

clue.text: Like a Young Conservative, quite quiet in quarry

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: quarry means prey, the hunted
pp, pianissimo, means very quiet in music

explanation.surface: A Young Tory, very quiet, hidden in a quarry pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarry' suggests a pit; it is what is hunted.
explanation.definitionFit: Preppy describes the neat, privileged style of young conservative types from smart schools.

clue.text: In haste to correct correction

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Rushing to put a mistake right.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is in haSTE To; 'to' is part of the run, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Proofreaders write the Latin for let it stand to cancel an earlier correction, a correction of a correction.

clue.text: Think of the kids!

definitions.meaning: a family's young, all the children

explanation.definitionFit: To brood is to ponder gloomily, and a brood is a family of young offspring.

clue.text: Defeat is counterproductive

indicators.note: productive is read as productive of something, so the letters of counter produce a new word

explanation.surface: Beating someone is said to backfire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counterproductive' is one word in the surface; split it, and 'productive' rearranges COUNTER. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce is to beat thoroughly, to defeat heavily.

clue.text: It makes my head spin before I turn green

indicators.note: before places the green word ahead of the rest

parts.note: vert is the heraldic word for green
a go is a turn

explanation.surface: Dizziness, then nausea turning me green.
explanation.walkthrough: Heraldry calls green VERT.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertigo is a sensation of whirling dizziness, so it makes one's head spin.

clue.text: Poem about cinema

parts.note: an ode is a poem
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A poem on the subject of the cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: The Odeon chain gave its name to cinemas generally in Britain.

clue.text: Composer's support for roses, not a bunch of freesias

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: not a means that letter is removed

parts.note: a pergola is a garden frame supporting climbing roses

indicators.note: a bunch of letters is taken from inside the flower name

explanation.surface: A composer's frame for roses lacks a bunch of freesias.
explanation.walkthrough: PERGOLA loses A; a bunch of freesias gives ESI from its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Battista Pergolesi was an 18th-century Italian composer of the Stabat Mater.
